identity.title: Learning Unmasking Policies for Diffusion Language Models

problem.claim: Design a sampling procedure that selects which tokens to unmask at each diffusion step in diffusion language models.

gap.claim: Heuristic unmasking strategies require manual tuning and their performance degrades with larger block sizes.

contributions.claim: Formalizes masked diffusion sampling as a Markov decision process and trains unmasking procedures with reinforcement learning.
Introduces a lightweight single-layer-transformer policy that maps dLLM token confidences to unmasking decisions.
Releases implementation code for the proposed approach.

stated_novelty.claim: The work replaces manually tuned heuristic sampling procedures with reinforcement-learned policies for masked diffusion sampling.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that trained policies match state-of-the-art heuristics when used with semi-autoregressive block generation.
The authors report that trained policies outperform the heuristics in the full-diffusion setting.
The authors report that prior confidence-thresholding heuristics improve sample quality and token throughput over random unmasking, but require manual tuning and degrade with larger block sizes.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion language models are described as matching autoregressive downstream performance on many tasks while potentially improving inference efficiency.
Sampling must determine which tokens to unmask at each diffusion step; confidence-based heuristics help but have tuning and block-size limitations.
The authors formulate masked diffusion sampling as an MDP and learn a lightweight confidence-to-decision policy with reinforcement learning.
The learned policies match heuristic performance for block generation and outperform heuristics under full diffusion.
Code is reported as publicly available.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a concrete heuristic failure mode—manual tuning and degradation with larger blocks—to an MDP formulation and a policy whose inputs and outputs are explicitly specified.

lessons.interpretation: A focused problem-to-method mapping can make a proposed learning-based replacement easy to evaluate conceptually.
lessons.application: When replacing a heuristic, state its operational limitation, formalize the decision process, and name the policy inputs and decisions before presenting comparisons.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the method does not make sequential decisions or when the heuristic limitation is not directly addressed by the proposed model.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, metrics, block sizes, reinforcement-learning setup, or quantitative margins behind the reported comparisons.
It does not identify which state-of-the-art heuristics were used as baselines or whether the reported results cover all stated task settings.
